description: Tests for content/platform/chainctl-usage/how-to-install-chainctl.md. The install tests read the page's code blocks at run time and run them in disposable Docker containers. token-cache-path needs you signed in to chainctl. The Homebrew install takes a few minutes, so raise the per-test cap: DOC_DETECTIVE_MAX_SECONDS=900 DOC_DETECTIVE_RETRIES=0 tests/doc-detective/console-cookie.sh --input tests/doc-detective/how-to-install-chainctl.spec.json

tests.description: The curl install works on a machine with only the prerequisites the page names: curl, plus sudo for the install step

steps.description: Start a fresh Ubuntu machine with curl and nothing else the page doesn't ask for
Run code block 1 of the introduction, as the page shows it
Run code block 1 of Install with curl, as the page shows it

runShell.command: python3 tests/doc-detective/code-blocks.py content/platform/chainctl-usage/how-to-install-chainctl.md 'Install with curl' 1 | tests/doc-detective/linux-machine.sh run doc-detective-chainctl-prerequisites tmp

steps.description: Run code block 2 of Install with curl, as the page shows it

runShell.command: python3 tests/doc-detective/code-blocks.py content/platform/chainctl-usage/how-to-install-chainctl.md 'Install with curl' 2 | tests/doc-detective/linux-machine.sh run doc-detective-chainctl-prerequisites tmp

steps.description: Start a fresh Ubuntu machine with chainctl 0.2.364 installed
Run the page's update command, answering Y when it asks whether to continue

steps.description: chainctl version reports the latest release

runShell.command: latest=$(curl -fsS https://dl.enforce.dev/chainctl/latest/metadata.json | jq -r .version) && echo chainctl version | tests/doc-detective/linux-machine.sh run doc-detective-chainctl-update | grep -E "^GitVersion: +$latest$"
